focus: Git 2.50.1's fsmonitor daemon lifecycle, and why a wedged daemon never recovers
noveltyJustification: Eleven of twelve findings are new to the packet: the man-page lifecycle, the ipcthreads default, the no-op Darwin health thread, the source-admitted infinite cookie wait and the unbounded client read were all unrecorded.
keyQuestions: Q1. What unset speckit.worktreeBase and removed the reaper's daemon handling, and does anything still create worktrees under .worktrees/ by default?
Q2. What is git 2.50.1's documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS, and how do fsmonitor.socketDir, idle shutdown and git fsmonitor--daemon stop behave when the daemon is wedged?
Q3. Is event overload the real cause of the hang, or is there a known daemon deadlock in this git version, for example around --ipc-threads or the cookie-file handshake?
Q4. Which call sites in the repo's hooks and scripts run git without a timeout, and which of them should opt out of fsmonitor?
Q5. What is the safest default: fsmonitor on with worktrees outside the checkout, or fsmonitor off for the main checkout and on per worktree?
answeredQuestions: Q2. What is git 2.50.1's documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS, and how do fsmonitor.socketDir, idle shutdown and git fsmonitor--daemon stop behave when the daemon is wedged?

ruledOut: --ipc-threads=8 is a repo or Apple tuning knob and the root cause
A git upgrade past 2.50.1 fixes the hang
Daemons exit on their own after idle time

graphEvents.label: Documented fsmonitor daemon lifecycle on macOS
No idle shutdown or self-exit is documented or implemented
The Darwin health thread is an empty stub
The daemon cookie handshake is an acknowledged infinite wait
The IPC client reply read has no deadline
